questions.question:
When two 8-bit numbers [latex]A_{7}....A_{0}[/latex] and [latex]B_{7}....B_{0}[/latex] in 2's complement representation (with [latex]A_{0}[/latex]
and [latex]B_{0}[/latex] as the least significant bits ) are added using a ripple-carry Combinational Circuit, the sum bits
obtained are  [latex]S_{7}....S_{0}[/latex] and the carry bits are  [latex]C_{7}....C_{0}[/latex]. An overflow is said to have occurred if
questions.explanation:
2's complement overflow happens when both operands have the same sign but the sum has the other sign:
- both negative ([latex]A_7=B_7=1[/latex]) and [latex]S_7=0[/latex], or
- both positive ([latex]A_7=B_7=0[/latex]) and [latex]S_7=1[/latex].

That is [latex]A_7B_7\bar S_7+\bar A_7\bar B_7S_7=1[/latex].

Answer: Option 3

Consider the following representation of a number in IEEE 754 single-precision floating point format with a bias of 127.

S:1
E:10000001
F:11110000000000000000000

Here, S,E and F denote the sign, exponent, and fraction components of the floating point representation.

The decimal value corresponding to the above representation (rounded to 2 decimal places) is ____________.
questions.explanation:
Exponent = 129 [latex]-[/latex] 127 = 2. Mantissa = 1.1111[latex]{}_2[/latex] = 1 + 0.5 + 0.25 + 0.125 + 0.0625 = 1.9375. Sign 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] negative.

Value [latex]=-1.9375\times2^2=-7.75[/latex]

Answer: -7.75

questions.question: In a system, numbers are represented using [latex]4[/latex]-bit two's complement form. Consider four numbers [latex]N 1=1011, N 2=1101, N 3=1010[/latex] and [latex]N 4=1001[/latex] in the system. Which of the following operations will result in arithmetic overflow?
questions.explanation:
Convert each 4-bit two's-complement number to its signed decimal value (invert bits and add [latex]1[/latex] if the leading bit is [latex]1[/latex]): [latex]N1{=}1011\to-5,\ N2{=}1101\to-3,\ N3{=}1010\to-6,\ N4{=}1001\to-7[/latex]. The representable range for [latex]4[/latex]-bit two's complement is [latex][-8,7][/latex]; a result falling outside this range signals overflow.

- [latex]N1+N2=-5+(-3)=-8[/latex] → within range. No overflow.
- [latex]N2+N3=-3+(-6)=-9[/latex] → below [latex]-8[/latex]. Overflow.
- [latex]N3-N4=-6-(-7)=1[/latex] → within range. No overflow.
- [latex]N1+N4=-5+(-7)=-12[/latex] → below [latex]-8[/latex]. Overflow.

Answer: N2+N3 and N1+N4 cause arithmetic overflow.

questions.question:
Consider three 4-variable functions [latex]f_1,f_2 \; and \; f_3[/latex], which are expressed in sum-of-minterms

[latex]f_1=\Sigma (0,2,5,8,14)[/latex]
[latex]f_2=\Sigma (2,3,6,8,14,15)[/latex]
[latex]f_3=\Sigma (2,7,11,14)[/latex]

For the following circuit with one AND gate and one XOR gate, the output function f can be expressed as:
questions.explanation:
Circuit: [latex]f=(f_1\cdot f_2)\oplus f_3[/latex].

- [latex]f_1\cdot f_2[/latex] = common minterms = {2, 8, 14}
- XOR with [latex]f_3[/latex] = {2, 7, 11, 14}: keep minterms in exactly one set [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 and 14 cancel, leaving {7, 8, 11}

Answer: [latex]\Sigma(7,8,11)[/latex]

questions.question:
Consider the real valued variables [latex]X, Y[/latex] and [latex]Z[/latex] represented using the IEEE [latex]754[/latex] singleprecision floating-point format. The binary representations of [latex]X[/latex] and [latex]Y[/latex] in hexadecimal notation are as follows:

[latex] X: 35 {C} 00000 \quad Y: 34 {A} 00000 [/latex]

Let [latex]Z=X+Y[/latex].

Which one of the following is the binary representation of [latex]Z[/latex], in hexadecimal notation?
questions.explanation:
Decode both IEEE-754 single-precision numbers (format: 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits [bias 127], 23 mantissa bits):

[latex]X=35\text{C}00000_{16}[/latex] → sign [latex]=0[/latex], exponent bits [latex]=01101011_2=107[/latex] (unbiased [latex]=107-127=-20[/latex]), mantissa [latex]=1.1_2[/latex]. So [latex]X=1.1_2\times2^{-20}[/latex].

[latex]Y=34\text{A}00000_{16}[/latex] → sign [latex]=0[/latex], exponent bits [latex]=01101001_2=105[/latex] (unbiased [latex]=-22[/latex]), mantissa [latex]=1.01_2[/latex]. So [latex]Y=1.01_2\times2^{-22}[/latex].

To add, align [latex]Y[/latex]'s exponent to [latex]-20[/latex] by shifting its mantissa right by [latex]2[/latex] bits: [latex]Y=0.0101_2\times2^{-20}[/latex].

[latex]X+Y=(1.1000_2+0.0101_2)\times2^{-20}=1.1101_2\times2^{-20}[/latex].

This is already normalized (leading digit [latex]1[/latex], no need to shift the exponent). So [latex]Z[/latex] has the same exponent as [latex]X[/latex] (exponent bits [latex]01101011[/latex]) and mantissa [latex]1101\underbrace{0\ldots0}_{19\text{ zeros}}[/latex], giving hex [latex]35\text{E}80000[/latex].

Answer: 35E80000

Click here for detail solution

questions.question:
A Boolean digital circuit is composed using two 4-input multiplexers (M1 and M2) and one 2-input multiplexer (M3) as shown in the figure. X0-X7 are the inputs of the multiplexers M1 and M2 and could be connected to either 0 or 1. The select lines of the multiplexers are connected to Boolean variables A, B and C as shown.

Which one of the following set of values of (X0, X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6, X7) will realise the Boolean function [latex] \bar{A}+\bar{A}\cdot \bar{C}+A\cdot \bar{B}\cdot C[/latex] ?
questions.explanation:
M1 and M2 use selects (A, C), so input index = 2A + C. M3 picks M1 when B = 0 and M2 when B = 1.

Simplify: [latex]F=\bar A+\bar A\bar C+A\bar BC=\bar A+A\bar BC[/latex]

- B = 0 (M1): A = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = 1 (X0 = X1 = 1); A = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = C (X2 = 0, X3 = 1)
- B = 1 (M2): A = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = 1 (X4 = X5 = 1); A = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = 0 (X6 = X7 = 0)

Answer: (1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0)

questions.question:
The number of min-terms after minimizing the following Boolean Algebra is _________.
[latex]{[{D}'+A{B}'+{A}'C+A{C}'D+{A}'{C}'{D}]}'[/latex]
questions.explanation:
Simplify inside the bracket:
- [latex]A\bar CD+\bar A\bar CD=\bar CD[/latex], and [latex]\bar D+\bar CD=\bar D+\bar C[/latex]
- [latex]\bar C+\bar AC=\bar C+\bar A[/latex]
- [latex]\bar A+A\bar B=\bar A+\bar B[/latex]

Inside = [latex]\bar A+\bar B+\bar C+\bar D[/latex], so its complement = ABCD, a single minterm.

Answer: 1

questions.question:
Consider a Boolean expression given by [latex] F(X, Y, Z)=\Sigma(3,5,6,7) [/latex].
Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

options.C: [latex] F(X, Y, Z) [/latex] is independent of input [latex] Y [/latex]
options.D: [latex] F(X, Y, Z) [/latex] is independent of input [latex] X [/latex]

questions.explanation:
Minterms 3, 5, 6, 7 = 011, 101, 110, 111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = 1 when at least two inputs are 1 (majority function).

- Maxterms are the remaining combinations: [latex]\Pi(0,1,2,4)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Majority function [latex]=XY+YZ+XZ[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Depends on Y: [latex]F(1,0,0)=0[/latex] but [latex]F(1,1,0)=1[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] so not independent of Y.
- Depends on X: [latex]F(0,1,0)=0[/latex] but [latex]F(1,1,0)=1[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] so not independent of X.

Answer: [latex]F=\Pi(0,1,2,4)[/latex] and [latex]F=XY+YZ+XZ[/latex]

questions.question:
Given the function F=P'+QR , where F is a function in three Boolean variables P,Q and R and P'=!P, consider the following statements.
(S1) F=[latex]\Sigma[/latex](4,5,6)
(S2) F=[latex]\Sigma[/latex](0,1,2,3,7)
(S3) F=[latex]\Pi[/latex](4,5,6)
(S4) F=[latex]\Pi[/latex](0,1,2,3,7)
Which of the following is true?
questions.explanation:
F = P' + QR is 1 for P = 0 (minterms 0, 1, 2, 3) and for P = Q = R = 1 (minterm 7).

- [latex]F=\Sigma(0,1,2,3,7)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S2 True, S1 False
- Maxterms are the rest: [latex]F=\Pi(4,5,6)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S3 True, S4 False

Answer: (S1) False, (S2) True, (S3) True, (S4) False
